stem: A neonatal unit registrar reviews a supine abdominal X-ray for possible bowel perforation; which finding most specifically supports free intraperitoneal gas on this view?

options.text: Football sign outlining the falciform ligament
Mosaic bowel gas pattern in a neonate

explanation: Football sign outlining the falciform ligament is the classic radiographic sign of free intraperitoneal gas on a supine abdominal X-ray.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 196

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because left lower lobe consolidation is a chest finding and does not indicate free intraperitoneal gas on an abdominal X-ray.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the football sign outlines the falciform ligament and is a named sign of free intraperitoneal gas.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a mosaic bowel gas pattern is described as a normal neonatal abdominal appearance rather than a sign of perforation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because dilated small bowel loops suggest obstruction, but they do not specifically identify free intraperitoneal gas.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a gasless abdomen suggests other pathology such as ascites and is not the specific sign of perforation-related free gas.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
